title: What to do after a gurobipy solve, from Status and SolCount

blocks.text: A crew-rostering service solves its MIP with gurobipy and must decide, after every solve, what to do with the result. All it has are two model attributes: `Status`, the optimization status code, and `SolCount`, the number of feasible plans Gurobi kept. Write `outcome(status, sol_count)`, which returns one of these strings:

Compare with the constants (`from gurobipy import GRB`), never with bare numbers. Importing gurobipy and reading its constants needs no license, so this practice runs without one. About fifteen lines.

from gurobipy import GRB


def outcome(status: int, sol_count: int) -> str:
    """What the caller does with a solve that ended with this Status and SolCount."""
    # TODO: OPTIMAL first, then the limit statuses (SolCount decides), then the "no plan" cases.
    return ""


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(outcome(GRB.OPTIMAL, 1), "|", outcome(GRB.TIME_LIMIT, 3), "|", outcome(GRB.INF_OR_UNBD, 0))

cases.says: a time, node or work limit with SolCount above 0 gives 'use, report gap', and with SolCount 0 gives 'no plan: limit'
INF_OR_UNBD gives its own answer, not the infeasible one
codes outside the table, such as NUMERIC or LOADED, give 'no plan: solver failure'
